dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Hello?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Hi Samer, it's Lina.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Hi Lina, what's new?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله تمام. كلمتك من شوية بس الخط كان مشغول
dialogue.transliteration: el-7amdu lillah tamaam. kallemtak min shwayya bass el-khaTT kaan mashghool
dialogue.english: All good, thank God. I called you a bit ago but the line was busy.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: أيوه، كنت بكلم أخويا. آسف إني ماعرفتش أرد عليكي
dialogue.transliteration: aywa, kunt bakallem akhuuya. aasef enni ma3rafteesh arudd 3aleeki
dialogue.english: Yeah, I was talking with my brother. Sorry I couldn't answer you.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمك. كنت عايزة أكلمك عن الميعاد
dialogue.english: Don't worry about it. I wanted to talk to you about the appointment.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: اتفضلي، بس ثانية واحدة، رصيدي هيخلص
dialogue.transliteration: etfaddali, bass saanya wa7da, raseedi hayekhlas
dialogue.english: Go ahead, just a second, my credit is about to run out.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: طيب خليني أقول بسرعة قبل ما الخط يقطع
dialogue.transliteration: Tayyeb khalleeni 2ool bisor3a 2abl ma el-khaTT ye2Ta3
dialogue.english: Okay, let me say it fast before the call gets cut off.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: لأ لأ، خلاص، اتقطع. ممكن تكلميني تاني بعد شوية؟
dialogue.transliteration: la2 la2, khalaas, et2aTa3. mumkin tekalmeeni taani ba3d shwayya?
dialogue.english: No no, that's it, it got cut off. Can you call me back in a bit?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: حاضر، كويس إنك رديت أصلاً. هكلمك تاني
dialogue.transliteration: 7aader, kwayyis ennak radeit aslan. hakallemak taani
dialogue.english: Sure, good that you picked up at all. I'll call you again.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Thanks, I'll wait for you.

pair.english: Can you call me back in a bit?

lessons.culture: In Cairo people answer with "ألو" and the caller says who they are with "معاك" plus a name, so "مين معايا؟" is what you ask when you do not know. A call usually opens with a few greetings such as "إزيك، إيه الأخبار" before the point, and jumping straight to business can sound abrupt.

exercises.prompt: You pick up a call from an unknown number. Answer and ask who is calling.

too_formal.item: السلام عليكم، من فضلك من المتصل؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct Arabic, but far more formal than the ordinary way of answering the phone.

exercises.tip: "ألو" opens a call and "مين معايا؟" asks who is on the line.

exercises.prompt: A friend on the phone asks: "إيه الأخبار؟". Say all is fine, thank God.

too_formal.item: الأمور على ما يرام ولله الحمد
too_formal.feedback: Correct but bookish; a spoken reply is much shorter.

exercises.tip: "الحمد لله" is almost always somewhere in the answer.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "ماعرفتش _____ عليك من شوية." Meaning: I couldn't answer you a bit ago.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "الخط _____ وأنا بكلمك." Meaning: The call got cut off while I was talking to you.

exercises.tip: "اتقطع" is the everyday word for a dropped call.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Egyptian Arabic: "My battery died."

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically fine, but far more formal than how people actually say it.

exercises.tip: "فصل" is what a phone does when its battery dies.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "There's no signal here."

too_formal.item: لا توجد تغطية شبكية في هذا المكان
too_formal.feedback: Correct but reads like a technician's report, not spoken Egyptian.

exercises.tip: "مفيش" means "there isn't" and "شبكة" is the network signal.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "My credit ran out"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but "خلص" is the everyday word, not "انتهى".

exercises.tip: "رصيد" is prepaid phone credit.

exercises.prompt: Which is the natural way to answer an incoming call?

too_formal.feedback: Too formal; nobody opens a phone call this way in Cairo.

exercises.tip: "ألو" answers the phone; the other phrases come once the call is going.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "مشغول / كان / الخط".

too_formal.feedback: That would be an unusual, technical way to say the line was busy.

exercises.tip: "الخط" comes right after "كان" here.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "شوية / بعد / تكلمني / تاني / ممكن".

too_formal.item: هل بإمكانك معاودة الاتصال بي لاحقاً
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but the formal written version, not the spoken order.

exercises.tip: "ممكن" opens the request, and "تاني" means "again".

reply.english: In front of the main entrance.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Lina, where should we meet tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Lina

dialogue.english: Don't be late on me, Lina.

lessons.culture: In Cairo people usually meet at a cafe or give a landmark such as a mosque or a metro station instead of a street address. Being a few minutes late is common, so a quick call to say you are on your way is normal and not rude.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks you: "نتقابل فين؟". Suggest meeting at the cafe.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct, but far more formal than a casual suggestion.

exercises.tip: "خلينا" plus a verb is the everyday way to suggest doing something together.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "الساعة كام تنفع معاك؟". Say that 7 o'clock works.

exercises.tip: "تنفع" is how a time "works" in Egyptian speech.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "هقابلك _____ البوابة الرئيسية." Meaning: I'll meet you in front of the main entrance.

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but "قدام" is what is actually said, not "أمام".

exercises.tip: "قدام" means "in front of" in everyday speech.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "لو _____ كلمني." Meaning: If you're late, call me.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but very formal written Arabic, not how it is said.

exercises.tip: "لو" plus a past-tense verb is the everyday "if".

exercises.prompt: Translate into Egyptian Arabic: "Don't be late."

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a formal written notice, not spoken Egyptian.

exercises.tip: "ما" before the verb and "ش" after it makes the everyday negative command.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'll be there before you."

exercises.tip: "ha" plus a verb makes the everyday future in Cairene speech.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks "What time suits you?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct but stiffer than the everyday spoken question.

exercises.tip: "كام" means "what number", so "الساعة كام" is "what time".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Let's meet at the cafe"?

too_formal.feedback: A correct classical form, but not how it is said in conversation.

exercises.tip: "خلينا" plus a verb is the everyday "let's".

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but far more elaborate than the short spoken question.

exercises.tip: The time comes first, then "تنفع" at the end.

challenge.title: A Phone Call to Rearrange Plans
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a phone conversation of at least 10 lines. It must include answering the phone, proposing a place and a time to meet, changing that plan for a real reason, agreeing on a new time or place, and, if the person you called is not free, leaving a message for someone else to pass on.
required_elements: Saying who is calling, using مين معايا or معاك plus a name.
A suggestion of where to meet, using خلينا نتقابل or a similar phrase.
A question about time, using الساعة كام تنفع or a similar phrase.
A reason for changing the plan, using حصلتلي ظروف or a similar phrase.
A request to postpone or change, using ينفع نأجل or ينفع نتقابل.
An apology for the change, using معلش، آسف or a similar phrase.
A reassurance in response, using ولا يهمك.
A closing thank-you, using شكراً أوي or تسلم.
At least one exchange about leaving or taking a message, using رسالة, قوله, or بلغه.

dialogue.transliteration: mafeesh mushkila, ne2aggel le-sab3a. ma3lesh, aasef enni ghayyart fag2a
dialogue.english: No problem, we'll postpone to 7. Sorry for the sudden change.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمك خالص. ولو مش هتعرف تيجي، ممكن أسيب رسالة مع أخوك؟
dialogue.transliteration: wala yhemmak khaales. we law mish hate3raf teegi, mumkin aseeb resaala ma3a akhuuk?
dialogue.english: Don't worry at all. And if you can't come, can I leave a message with your brother?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: أكيد، هقوله. شكراً أوي على صبرك
dialogue.english: Sure, I'll tell him. Thanks a lot for your patience.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: You're welcome, see you at 7.
